title: Silas and the Tide
premise: Silas Ashgrove, a pastry chef on the edge of losing his café, joins a court-mandated restorative justice program as an anonymous pen-pal to the man who destroyed his family twelve years ago—without either knowing the other's identity. As letters deepen into intimacy, Silas realizes he's falling for the very person he swore to condemn, while his correspondent, ex-convict Jonah Vane, is quietly working to make amends he believes are impossible. When identities are revealed at the program's final hearing, Silas must choose between the rehearsed sentence of vengeance and an unscripted truth; he speaks not for punishment but for a future neither man planned, and they build something fragile and real together as the café—and their lives—are saved by honesty rather than law.
about_author: Rosalind Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town baker turned novelist who writes love stories about people learning to be seen. She lives on a windswept coast where she collects tide charts and insists all her characters deserve second proofings.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Opening in the pre-dawn kitchen of Ashgrove's café, we learn the bank's final notice sits under the flour tin and that Silas measures life in safe increments since a fire twelve years ago took his father's bakery and his family's name. Emotional beat: quiet dread masked by routine.

chapters.title: The Letter That Finds You
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A court liaison delivers the Restorative Correspondence Initiative assignment: write anonymously to an offender seeking accountability. Silas signs up half out of spite, half desperation for the stipend. Emotional beat: brittle resolve—he tells himself this is about justice, nothing else.

chapters.title: Inmate 4471
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inside Halloway Correctional, Jonah Vane, eleven months from parole, receives his first letter and recognizes the bitterness in it as something earned, not performed. He answers honestly for the first time in years. Emotional beat: wary hope meeting guarded anger across paper.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Letters begin trading recipes for confessions: Silas describes bread as memory, Jonah describes fire as the worst thing he ever learned to make. Neither names the crime. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness threading through hostility.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Flashback to the night of the fire—the verdict, the plea deal, the sentence Silas never got to say aloud because the case settled. His sister Mara urges him to drop the letters; he can't. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: What Jonah Burned
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We learn Jonah was nineteen, hired to torch the bakery as insurance fraud by the man who owned the debt—Silas's uncle. Jonah has carried this alone, believing no one would believe him. Emotional beat: shame curdling into a decision to finally tell the truth.

chapters.title: Sunday Proofing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A near-encounter: Jonah, on supervised work release, comes into the café. They speak for four minutes without knowing each other. Silas finds himself charmed against his will. Emotional beat: the first crack in the wall between enemy and person.

chapters.title: Letters We Didn't Mean
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The correspondence turns intimate—fears, loneliness, the shape of forgiveness. Both catch themselves waiting for the mail. Emotional beat: falling in love disguised as accountability.

chapters.title: Mara Reads One
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Mara discovers a letter and reads enough to recognize details of the fire. She demands Silas end it, revealing she's been paying the café's debts secretly to keep him from drowning. Emotional beat: loyalty colliding with truth inside the family.

chapters.title: The Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah writes the full truth—his employer, the uncle, the setup—but hesitates to send it, fearing it will only wound Silas deeper. His parole hearing approaches and the program requires disclosure. Emotional beat: courage stalling at the threshold.

chapters.title: Payment Due
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The bank calls the loan; the café has thirty days. A developer offers to buy him out—the same development company whose name makes Jonah's blood run cold. Emotional beat: desperation narrowing every choice.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Released early to a halfway house, Jonah takes work nearby, telling himself it's coincidence. He watches Silas through the café window each morning, unable to enter or stay away. Emotional beat: longing shadowed by deception.

chapters.title: Coffee, Black, No Name
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Jonah finally walks in; they talk like strangers becoming friends over three afternoons. Silas feels guilty—betraying his pen-pal with real-world warmth. Emotional beat: two halves of one affection unknowingly converging.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Shadow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The developer pressuring Silas is the uncle's old partner, still laundering money through property. Jonah realizes the fire was never just about insurance—it was about silencing Silas's father, who'd found the books. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Someone torches the café's back storeroom—a warning. Insurance balks; police shrug. Silas, standing in wet ash, feels twelve years collapse. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible familiarity.

chapters.title: Reveal
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the program's final facilitated hearing, envelopes open: Silas learns his pen-pal is the arsonist; Jonah learns his correspondent is the son. The room goes silent. Silas walks out. Emotional beat: devastation—the cruelest cliffhanger of identity.

chapters.title: The Sentence Spoken
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Alone with the rehearsed condemnation, Silas instead returns and asks the question he's never asked: why? Jonah gives him the letter he never sent—the uncle, the books, the silencing. Emotional beat: vengeance dissolving into unbearable clarity.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Mara begs him to let it go; the uncle's partner offers to erase the debt if Silas stays quiet. Silas must choose between protecting his sister's fragile peace and exposing the truth. Emotional beat: the cost of justice made personal.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Silas and Jonah go together to the state attorney with the old ledger pages Jonah kept hidden. The investigation reopens; the developer is arrested. Silas publicly forgives—not excusing, but releasing. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law finally served by truth.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Rising
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The community, moved by the story, crowds the reopened café; Mara and Silas reconcile over dough at midnight. Jonah waits outside, unsure of his welcome. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt from ruin.

chapters.title: First Day, Second Chance
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Silas hires him—not as charity but because he's good with his hands and better with honesty now. First day of work, first time they're on the same side of the counter. Emotional beat: tentative joy, love admitted aloud at last.

chapters.title: Silas and the Tide
chapters.summary: Both POVs, epilogue. One year later: the café thrives, the trial concluded, and the two men walk the shore at dawn where Silas once rehearsed his sentence. He says a different one now—I choose you. Emotional beat: peace; the tide that took everything brings them home.
